title: Braised Cabbage with Apple and Balsamic
subtitle: Slow-cooked cabbage with apple, honey, and vinegar
excerpt: This is a British and German staple for autumn and winter tables. White cabbage slowly braises in vinegar and honey until it turns silky and deeply flavoured. Balsamic vinegar adds colour and depth.
sourceNotes: Braised red or white cabbage with apple and vinegar is common to British, German, and Scandinavian tables. The long, slow cook is traditional.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently in a covered pan.
recipe.batchNotes: Makes excellent leftovers. The flavour deepens on the second day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently before serving.

content.text: Low heat and a tight lid are all this needs. Do not rush the cooking time. The cabbage will seem like far too much at the start; it shrinks significantly as it braises.
Melt the butter in the stockpot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the shredded cabbage, grated apple, cinnamon, and cloves. Stir well to combine.
Add both vinegars, the honey, and 100ml of water. Season well with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce to the lowest heat. Cover tightly and cook for 50 to 60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes.

Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes if there is excess liquid. The cabbage should be silky and almost dry. Remove the cloves before serving. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more vinegar or honey.

items.symptom: The cabbage has caught and is catching on the bottom.
items.cause: Too little liquid or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Add a splash of water and reduce heat immediately.

items.cause: Too much vinegar relative to honey.
items.fix: Add another tablespoon of honey and stir through.

items.symptom: The cabbage is still slightly crunchy after 60 minutes.
items.fix: Continue cooking for 20 more minutes with the lid on.
